title: GRAP-III Curbs Imposed in Delhi-NCR as Air Nears Severe Ahead of Diwali
excerpt: The CAQM invoked Stage III on November 6: non-essential construction is banned, BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel cars are restricted, and several Delhi stations are already in the severe zone.
body:
• The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) invoked GRAP Stage III across Delhi-NCR on Friday, November 6, 2026, as a precautionary measure ahead of Diwali.
  • Delhi's overall AQI was 389 in the very poor category at 8 a.m., with IIT Delhi and Rohini at 474, Punjabi Bagh at 465 and RK Puram at 443 — all in the severe zone.
  • Non-essential construction and demolition are banned, stone crushers and mining are halted, and BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel four-wheelers face restrictions in Delhi and five NCR districts.
  • State governments may shift classes up to Class V to hybrid mode; Stage I and II measures remain in force underneath the new curbs.

Delhi-NCR moved to stricter pollution controls on Friday after the Commission for Air Quality Management invoked Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan, known as GRAP-III, as a precautionary measure ahead of Diwali. The decision was taken by the CAQM sub-committee on GRAP on November 6, according to Jagran's report of the announcement, which the commission also posted on X.

How bad the air is

The city's average AQI was recorded at 389, in the very poor category, at 8 a.m. on Friday, according to Central Pollution Control Board data cited by 7Globe. Jagran put the overall reading at 382 at 4 a.m. Several monitoring stations were already in the severe zone: IIT Delhi and Rohini topped the list at 474 each, followed by Punjabi Bagh at 465, RK Puram at 443, ITO at 422, Firoz Shah Road at 420 and India Gate at 403. Municipal authorities deployed truck-mounted water sprinklers around India Gate as part of dust-control measures.

What changes under Stage III

The Stage III package sits on top of the Stage I and II measures already in force. Its main elements, as reported by Jagran, are a strict ban on non-essential construction and demolition across Delhi-NCR; a halt to stone crusher operations and mining; restrictions on BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel four-wheelers in Delhi and in Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Gautam Buddha Nagar and Sonipat; restrictions on certain inter-state diesel buses entering Delhi, with exemptions for cleaner-fuel and compliant vehicles; restricted entry for specified non-BS-VI diesel light and medium goods vehicles registered outside Delhi; a prohibition on non-compliant brick kilns and hot-mix plants; and intensified mechanical sweeping and water sprinkling with dust suppressants. State governments may also consider shifting classes up to Class V to hybrid mode, with students attending physically or online.

Why it was invoked before the severe mark

GRAP Stage III is the plan's severe-category stage, and the CAQM described this invocation as precautionary — imposed while the citywide average was still in the very poor band but with multiple stations already severe and Diwali, with its firework load, immediately ahead. The India Meteorological Department forecasts shallow fog over the next four days, transitioning to early morning fog or mist on November 10-11, conditions that typically trap pollutants near the ground.

What to watch

The curbs stay in force until the CAQM reviews air quality again. For residents and for the many diaspora families arriving in Delhi this week, the practical points are the vehicle restrictions — an older petrol or diesel car that was legal on Thursday may be restricted now — and the possibility of hybrid classes for younger children. If readings push deeper into the severe band, the next step in the plan is Stage IV, which carries tighter vehicle and office measures.
